name: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
problem: For long-content generation the KV cache stored in GPU memory scales linearly with sequence length and batch size, adding a large transient-memory cost on top of model parameters.
mechanism: The observation: a small subset of tokens (HEAVY HITTERS) contributes most of the attention value, and their emergence correlates with token co-occurrence in the text. H2O then maintains an accumulated-attention score per token and EVICTS the lowest-scoring entries whenever the cache is full, subject to a theoretical guarantee under mild assumptions. Locality is preserved by combining recent-window tokens with historical heavy hitters.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): with 20% heavy hitters, throughput improves over DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, HuggingFace Accelerate and FlexGen by up to 29x, 29x and 3x respectively on OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B; and at the SAME batch size, latency reduced by up to 1.9x. Read the three multipliers carefully - the 29x figures are against specific serving systems and reflect the memory freed for batching, while 1.9x is the same-batch-size latency comparison and is the more conservative number.
